candidate.blueprint_locator: Safety and Infection Prevention and Control — hand hygiene, standard precautions, and prevention of cross-contamination
candidate.blueprint_topic: Safety and Infection Prevention and Control — glove changes between tasks
candidate.educational_objective: Prevent cross-contamination by changing gloves and performing hand hygiene when moving from dirty to clean care on the same client.

options.A: Keep the same gloves because the client has not changed
options.B: Remove the soiled gloves, perform hand hygiene, and don clean gloves if the next task requires them
options.C: Keep the same gloves as long as no second client is touched
options.D: Change gloves only when moving from one client to another

candidate.rationale: CDC guidance directs healthcare workers to change gloves and clean hands when moving from a soiled body site or contaminated task to a clean body site/task on the same patient. Gloves are not a substitute for hand hygiene. B is correct.
candidate.source_claim_supported: Healthcare workers should change gloves and perform hand hygiene when moving from soiled/contaminated care to clean care on the same patient.
candidate.source_document_title: Clinical Safety: Hand Hygiene for Healthcare Workers
candidate.source_locator: Know when to change gloves and clean hands — moving from a soiled body site to a clean body site on the same patient
candidate.source_organization: Centers for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC)
candidate.stem: After completing contaminated wound care, a nurse must perform a clean task for the same client. What should the nurse do before beginning the clean task?
